title: Missing Fraction Part Word Problems
intro: Keep the same reference whole when teaching missing fraction amounts.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Represent the total and known part on matching fraction strips. Identify the unfilled part before subtracting.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

3/2 + □ = 2

Two unit wholes make four halves: 2 = 4/2. Three halves are known, leaving one half.

2 − 3/2 = 4/2 − 3/2 = 1/2

Check: 3/2 + 1/2 = 4/2 = 2.

Ask your student

What do the known part and the missing part add up to?

If your student needs help

If the student's pieces use different wholes, redraw the strips at the same scale.
